newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip marginally in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip marginally in quiet market.

text.p: Danish bond prices eased slightly on Tuesday on a quiet market still closely watching events at the European Union summit in Amsterdam.
"Prices have fallen back a little, but the market did seem overbought. Otherwise, it has been very quiet," a dealer said.
At 1110 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.15, yielding 6.15 percent, down 0.15 point from Monday in turnover of about one billion crowns.
The seven percent 2007 bond slipped 0.11 point to 104.76, yielding 6.35 percent, in turnover of 600 million crowns.
The crown eased to 3.8068 to the mark from Monday's 3.8064.
The 2006 yield gap with Germany narrowed to 45 basis points from Monday's 46 bp, and the 2007 gap to the bund was unchanged at 65 bp.
The 2006's September future fell 0.04 point to 111.24 and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 slipped 0.07 to 90.28.

The central bank sold an estimated 500 million crowns of mainly short and medium-term paper. The bank said on Tuesday that it would continue sales of existing bonds, bills and treasury notes in the second half of 1997 and would open a series of 10-month treasury bills on June 27.
